scenario.label: A hazard scenario sigma is a set of active hazard zones and a set of closed roads; the open road graph drops the closed roads.

demand.label: An origin evacuates its whole population when it lies in an active hazard zone, and nobody otherwise.

capacity.label: A floor area of F square meters holds F divided by 3.5, rounded down; a 63 square meter classroom holds 18.

tiers.tex: c^{0}_s = C\big(F^{ec}_s\big),\quad c^{1}_s = C\big(F^{open}_s\big),\quad c^{2}_s = q\,k_s
tiers.label: Each shelter splits into three tiers: non-school space, school open space, and classrooms at 18 per room.

plan.label: A plan places no more vulnerable persons than an origin has, and no more persons in a tier than it holds.

lex.label: Lexicographic order: most vulnerable placed, then most persons placed, then fewest in classrooms, then fewest in school open spaces, then fewest person-minutes of travel.

penalties.label: The penalty weights that turn the lexicographic order into one minimum-cost flow.

vector.label: In the app each trip costs a vector: one if it ends in a classroom, one if it ends in a school open space, and its minutes, compared in that order.

rooms.label: Classrooms closed at a school are its classroom evacuees over 18, rounded up; learners displaced add up the learners of those rooms; classroom-days multiply by the stay.

packing.label: Packing closes at most one classroom more than the true minimum for each school in use beyond the first.

monotone.label: A higher alert level never frees classrooms.

expanded.label: In the time-expanded network a road moves up to its capacity each minute and takes its travel time; anyone may wait in place.

clearance.label: The clearance time is the first minute by which everyone the plan moves can be inside a shelter.

lowerbound.label: Lower bound: the shortest trip minus one plus the evacuees over the static flow rate, rounded up, and never below the longest nearest-shelter trip.

closure.label: Closing a set of roads B never shortens the clearance time.

siting.label: The siting gain of new centers S is how many more evacuees can be sheltered outside classrooms within theta minutes.

submod.tex: f(S \cup \{j\}) - f(S) \;\ge\; f(T \cup \{j\}) - f(T),\quad S \subseteq T
submod.label: Submodular: a new site adds at least as much to a smaller set of sites as to a larger one.

greedy.label: The greedy choice of k sites reaches at least 1 minus (1 minus 1 over k) to the k, and so at least 63.2 percent, of the best possible gain.

sphere.label: Seven meters by nine meters, at 3.5 square meters per person, is 18 evacuees per classroom.
